eligibility.quote: This issue happens when a single node subscribes to a topic multiple times and each subscriber has a different message type.

failed_conditions.quote: The program crashes as soon as the second `create_subscription` call is made.

loudness.quote:
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'rclcpp::exceptions::RCLError'
  what():  could not create subscription: failed to create topic, at /tmp/binarydeb/ros-eloquent-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp-0.4.4/src/rmw_node.cpp:1446, at /tmp/binarydeb/ros-eloquent-rcl-0.8.4/src/rcl/subscription.c:168

resolution.quote: @pjreed this problem should have disappeared about two weeks ago with #114 getting merged (certainly for a build from source, I don't know if the binary packages have been updated yet). I'd appreciate it if you could confirm this before closing the issue.

notes: Independently verified: issue body states version 0.4.4-1bionic.20200121.221538, rviz2 with Pose and Marker displays on /test, "Note that FastRTPS behaves correctly." (so the refusal does not occur with any correct peer — not internal), "This bug also exists with the binary version in ROS Dashing.", and the RCLError console output verbatim. Maintainer (eboasson): "From the description, this is a duplicate of #72, which got fixed for Foxy (https://github.com/eclipse-cyclonedds/cyclonedds/pull/382 and #96)." The reporter could only test an older binary ("I see in that `package.xml` file that it's version `0.5.1`, although the latest version of `ros-dashing-rmw-cyclonedds-cpp` in the apt repository is `0.4.2-1bionic.20200318.032607` ... I tested that and it still crashes."). Class: nominal_type_mismatch (two nominal types requested on one topic name, refused by the provider's per-participant one-type-per-topic binding) is defensible and the spec itself discusses the exclusive_resource_conflict alternative in notes; the primary refusal text ("failed to create topic") supports either, so I do not overturn. Loudness: loud_documented/activate is right — the runtime refuses the second subscription at entity creation with an explicit rcl error that crashes the process; that is a diagnostic at activation of the interface element, not a silent run-time effect. Resolution: recommended is right — the fix was never shown working in this composition (maintainer asked for confirmation, none arrived; the issue was closed later by age per the spec's citation of clalancette's closing comment, which I take from the spec since I did not re-fetch that line).
